title: Argentina 7-0 Costa Rica: Paz, Alvarez and Mastantuono all double up in rout
subtitle: Nico Paz, Julian Alvarez and Franco Mastantuono each scored twice as Argentina hammered Costa Rica 7-0 in their final match of 2026.
paragraphs: Argentina capped off 2026 in magnificent style as they thrashed Costa Rica 7-0, with a trio of players each scoring twice.
Nico Paz continued his stellar form with a first-half double, while Julian Alvarez also netted twice before the break.
Paz's half-time replacement Franco Mastantuono scored a second-half brace, with those goals coming either side of an effort from Alexis Mac Allister.

Argentina were in front with just eight minutes on the clock. Alvarez charged down the right and picked out Enzo Fernandez, whose backheel found Paz, and the Como star nailed a finish into the top corner.
Alvarez went close to a quickfire second, though Costa Rica did offer some threat at the other end through Josimar Mendez, but Argentina were 2-0 up in the 35th minute.
Agustin Giay got in down the right wing and played it in for Alvarez, who finished first-time.
Gianluca Prestianni hit the woodwork within moments of play restarting, and Argentina got their third in the 38th minute when Paz capped a brilliant run with a stunning strike.

Alvarez hammered into the roof of the net five minutes later, and just three minutes into the second half, substitute Mastantuono got in on the act when his effort was bundled in by Costa Rica goalkeeper Patrick Sequeira.
Mac Allister pounced on Gerald Taylor's loose pass to make it 6-0, before Mastantuono completed the scoring with a magnificent seventh in the 88th minute.
Argentina missed Lionel Messi in last week's defeat to Uruguay, and Lionel Scaloni's team can no longer rely on the magic of their mercurial number 10.
And while Messi's absence will surely be felt again, this is a new era for Argentina, and in Paz, they have one of the most exciting prospects in world football on their hands.

He had four shots, a tally matched by Alvarez but bettered by Jose Manuel Lopez, but both of Paz's goals were of the highest quality, as evidenced by the fact his four attempts overall were only worth a combined 0.17 expected goals. The youngster also won all four of the duels he contested.

This was a welcome return to form for Alvarez, meanwhile. He has had a tough time of it at Atletico Madrid this term following the transfer saga surrounding him this summer, but he led the game for touches in the opposition box (12) and chances created (three).

It was complete dominance from the hosts at Estadio Mario Alberto Kempes, as Argentina posted 75.6% possession and 22 shots, though they did wildly overperform their 1.78 xG, showing the high calibre of their finishing.

Elsewhere, in-form Uruguay made light work of the Dominican Republic, winning 5-0, with four of those goals coming after the 70th minute. They have now won their last four matches by an aggregate score of 17-3.
